shouldFix.title: Three /sources paths changed without any repairLog operation naming them, falsifying basedOn.method; two of the three are edits to historical measurement notes the artifact's own discipline says are not rewritten
detail: basedOn.method asserts: 'Every path the v7 repairLog (V6-S1, CLAUDE-V6-A1, CLAUDE-V6-A4, CLAUDE-V6-A5, CODEX-V6-A1, META-v7) does not name is unchanged from v6.' I extracted every path named across all six entries' operations: /artifact, /version, /basedOn, /appliesFindingsOf, /reviewGuidance/forTheIndependentReviewer, /whatThisDoesNotDo/1, /rejectionRules/rules/3/trigger, /lockSchema/fields/1/semantics, /sources/corpusHeadAtAuthoring, and /sources/bindingSources[SRC-PROTO]/verifiedAtAuthoring plus custodyCaveats. My recursive diff found 30 changed paths. Three are not in that set.

UNNAMED 1 - /sources/reMeasurementAtV7, an ADDED key carrying substantive custody content: 'Predecessor is v6 51b0a0b7...; bindingSources whole-document digests remain v2-authoring measurements. Live pins unchanged from reMeasurementAtV6: SRC-08 1cdcf9d4...; SRC-D 12d192f7...; SRC-FRZ e809d439... SRC-02 and SRC-03 still match their recorded v2 hashes.' No operation adds it. This is a regression against v6's own practice: the equivalent key there was added by an explicit operation, 'ADD /sources/reMeasurementAtV6', under V5-S1.
UNNAMED 2 - /sources/reMeasurementAtV2, CHANGED. Its closing sentence was rewritten from 'corpusHeadAtAuthoring is the v2 authoring head' to 'corpusHeadAtV2Authoring is the v2 authoring head'.

UNNAMED 3 - /sources/reMeasurementAtV5, CHANGED. Its opening was rewritten from 'HISTORICAL: corpusHeadAtAuthoring and reMeasurementAtV2 remain v2-era measurements' to 'HISTORICAL: corpusHeadAtV2Authoring and reMeasurementAtV2 remain v2-era measurements'.

The CLAUDE-V6-A5 operation reads 'AMEND /sources/corpusHeadAtAuthoring - renamed corpusHeadAtV2Authoring'. That covers the key's own removal and re-addition, which is the same rename pattern v6 used for measuredAtAuthoring, and I accept it as naming both ends. It does not name the two cross-reference edits in other paths. This is the standard the chain has already set for itself: Codex's v3 B2 required 'every edit explicit at resolving JSON-Pointer paths, including metadata and each independently motivated array-member/string edit'.
shouldFix.secondAspect: Two of the three unnamed changes mutate HISTORICAL records. /sources/reMeasurementAtV2 is a record of what was measured at v2 authoring and now asserts that 'corpusHeadAtV2Authoring is the v2 authoring head' - naming a field that did not exist at v2 authoring. /sources/reMeasurementAtV5 is likewise a v5-era note now written in v7's vocabulary. The artifact established the opposite discipline explicitly at v6's V5-B2 entry - 'The v5 repairLog entry V4-S2 is left byte-identical (historical; no landed repair is rewritten)' - and v7 itself leans on that discipline by carrying repairLog[0:44] byte-identical. Rewriting historical notes to match a current field name is defensible bookkeeping, but it is a choice that should be stated, not made silently.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The repairLog-as-complete-diff-account is the mechanism a reviewer relies on to trust a successor without re-deriving it, and it is the single most-repaired property in this chain: it produced Codex B2 at v3, V4-S1 at v4, and V5-A1 plus CLAUDE-V5-S1 at v5. v6 achieved it cleanly at 48-for-48. v7 regresses to 27-for-30. Nothing substantive is hidden - all three changes are correct and I verified reMeasurementAtV7's empirical content independently - but the completeness sentence is false as written, and a reviewer who trusted it would not have looked at these paths.
shouldFix.remedy: Add an operation under CLAUDE-V6-A5 naming /sources/reMeasurementAtV2 and /sources/reMeasurementAtV5 as rename cross-reference updates, with a clause stating that historical notes are updated for name resolution only; and add 'ADD /sources/reMeasurementAtV7' under META-v7, matching how reMeasurementAtV6 was accounted at v6.

advisories.title: whatThisDoesNotDo[1] hedges on fixture existence where the measured fact was available and non-binding
advisories.detail: The repaired clause says a fixture-corpus candidate 'may exist in the tree'. It does exist: docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/dr-103/ holds 64 files, and Codex's V6-S1 detail supplied the candidate's digest d81a4ef9ed26405a07e84ae0be9a3d2048fd9a6126b1f93d139a5a499204b542 with its 51 authored plus 13 supporting-byte counts. Nothing in v7 is false - a hedge is not a false claim, and keeping deliberate distance from an unreviewed candidate is defensible for an artifact that must not appear to accept or apply it. But the artifact elsewhere prefers measured statements to hedges, and a precise non-binding reference ('a candidate exists at <digest>; it is not accepted, qualified, or applied here') would have been both true and stronger. This is the same hedge-versus-measure pattern that was a real defect at v5's 'may have moved' source pins; here it costs nothing because no claim is wrong.
advisories.notBlocking: No false statement. The non-qualification boundary is stated correctly and is strengthened over v6.

advisories.title: The carry reason routes a schema-shape decision to a corpus milestone without naming an owning row
advisories.detail: notFoldedThisSuccessor says normalization of the corpus-class container shape may happen 'after SATISFIED-GRADE corpus review'. That names a milestone, not an owner. Everywhere else this artifact routes deferred work to a register row or identity dependency by id - DR-111, DR-112, DR-114, DR-120, ID-DEP-1 through ID-DEP-12, and OD-1 for the caps question. CLAUDE-V6-A2 and CLAUDE-V6-A3 remain open with no row carrying them, so they can only be recovered by reading this successor's prose. Naming the owning surface, or recording them as a named open decision the way OD-1 already models, would keep them findable.
advisories.notBlocking: The findings are advisories, are explicitly recorded as open, and the deferral rationale (avoiding a V5-B1-class enumeration regression) is sound.

Claude 2 v6: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, blockers [], shouldFix [], advisories [V6-A1..V6-A5]; v7's claude2V6 record states precisely that, and I confirm as its author. The idCollisionNote is accurate: my V6-A1 (RJ-4 lock-arm marker) is not Codex's V6-A1 (total tuple comparator), and the repairLog disambiguates them as CLAUDE-V6-A1 and CODEX-V6-A1.
